CFD-accuracy-only wins and second-shader-dialect features must clear a high bar. Add a pure-TS reducer gridScaleEnergyFraction(field, w, h, components) to src/lib/engine/__benches__/reducers.ts: energy of (field minus a 3x3 box-smoothed field) divided by total field energy — the fraction of energy living at grid scale. Then a browser test (e.g. src/lib/engine/__benches__/grid-scale.browser.test.ts) that, for each bench scene (dipole/kelvinHelmholtz/rayleighBenard/thinWallTeslaValve) and a couple representative decorative preset configs, runs advance() deterministically, readField('velocity'), and asserts gridScaleEnergyFraction stays within a per-scene band (well below a churn threshold). Reuses the merged Phase-0 harness; no PNGs, no cross-renderer determinism problem, no new runtime deps.

tasks.title: [HUMAN/DESIGN] ADR: cross-renderer determinism + diff metric + update-goldens workflow
tasks.spec: Write the ADR that makes the full golden-image gate buildable WITHOUT shipping flaky. Decide on paper: (1) cross-renderer determinism — goldens generated by the EXACT CI renderer (headless-Chromium SwiftShader), since the chaotic float pipeline differs across renderers (local Apple Metal vs CI); contributors cannot regen locally. (2) A CI update-goldens workflow_dispatch job that regenerates+commits PNGs, plus a SEPARATE Playwright visual CI job (not the default green-gate, per ADR-0042). (3) A tolerant/structural diff metric (downsample + in-repo SSIM for zero deps, OR pixelmatch as a devDep) tuned to absorb SwiftShader jitter yet still catch grid-scale churn. (4) An intra-run determinism self-check (render a preset twice in one process, byte-identical) as the precondition for trusting any golden.
acceptance: A committed ADR answering (1)-(4); flags renderer jitter as the top operational risk; requires run-to-run stability over ~5 CI runs before the gate becomes required.
constraints: Design only — do this EARLY/in parallel so only the golden CAPTURE waits on retunes. The make-or-break of the whole golden-image item; do not write golden code before it exists.
tasks.note: All lenses flagged the undesigned determinism/regen workflow as the #1 risk — the classic flaky gate everyone disables. Decide it first.

tasks.title: [CUT] Multigrid / V-cycle pressure tier
tasks.spec: NOT building this. Unanimous across all 3 lenses: (1) Wrong direction vs the one measurement we have — ADR-0038 proved the pressure loop is pass/encoder-overhead bound at shipping grids (sim 128-192); a V-cycle is strictly MORE passes, predicted to LOSE frame-time at the only grids the library ships (its win lives in the fragment-bound 768-class regime mobile never reaches). (2) Zero decorative value — under-convergence reads as faint low-frequency divergence near obstacles, invisible/acceptable in the smooth dye look; only 4 desktop-only flow presets could even theoretically benefit, on CFD grounds the aesthetic ignores. (3) Doubly gated — hard-depends on the deferred Phase 3. (4) High regression risk, human-QA-only detection.
constraints: If a REAL reproduced pressure under-convergence complaint on a shipping preset ever lands, the answer is the CHEAP convergence ladder (more iterations -> Chebyshev / red-black Jacobi -> ONE two-grid smoother) as a small demand-gated item — NOT a multigrid tier.
